# My other projects in detail ## MindBridge: RAG-based student wellbeing chatbot (2026) MindBridge is a chatbot I built to support homesick students. It is a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system, built with Python, FAISS, Flan-T5, Groq/Llama and Gradio. I benchmarked a Flan-T5 model against a Groq Llama RAG pipeline to see which gave better, safer answers. I also built a 5-level stress classification system that ranges from mild to severe stress, and it reached a 98% safe-response accuracy rate. For evaluation I created an 80-question benchmark dataset spread over 7 files, plus an HTML-based evaluation frontend so I can compare the two models side by side. The hardest part of MindBridge was the API configuration. ## Campus Marketplace: full-stack mobile app (2026) Campus Marketplace is a 4-role, multi-campus marketplace app built with React Native, Expo, Supabase and Node.js. I built the Campus Admin portal end to end, which is 23 of the 54 screens, going from Figma designs all the way to production code. I implemented a shared design system and theming architecture that is reused across all the admin screens, which made the UI more consistent and development faster. # SentinelGuard: my final year project ## The big picture My final year project (FYP) is a smart industrial control system: a zero trust framework for IoT devices, with a focus on reliability. I prefer not to share more detail about the wider project. We are a group of 4 people. The part I'm working on is called SentinelGuard. ## What SentinelGuard is SentinelGuard is an IoT-based automated safety and liquid control system. It monitors the fluid level in physical tanks and automates pump and valve operations in real time. ## How it's built The system is built around an ESP32 microcontroller, relay modules and ultrasonic sensors. The ultrasonic sensors measure how full a tank is, the ESP32 decides what to do, and the relay modules switch the pumps and valves on and off. Data moves over the MQTT protocol, which is lightweight and works well for IoT devices. The system uses custom setpoints, so the operator can choose the levels at which pumps and valves act. It also has fail-safe rules, so that overflows and system failures are prevented even when something goes wrong. Everything is controlled through a custom operator console interface. ## Why reliability matters The goal
